# macOS release signing

1. Set the GitHub repository variable `NEXUS_MAC_TEAM_ID` to the Apple Team ID. Publish a bridge release on the update channels you support while the workflow is still using `MAC_SIGNING_CERT_P12` and `MAC_SIGNING_CERT_PASSWORD`. Confirm that an older install can update to the bridge in place.
2. Give users time to install the bridge. Then add `MAC_DEVELOPER_ID_CERT_P12`, `MAC_DEVELOPER_ID_CERT_PASSWORD`, `MAC_NOTARY_API_KEY_P8`, `MAC_NOTARY_API_KEY_ID`, and `MAC_NOTARY_API_ISSUER`. Use base64 for the `.p12` and `.p8` files. Use a Developer ID Application certificate for the same Apple team and an App Store Connect team API key with an issuer ID. With all five secrets in place, the next release uses Developer ID and notarization. Keep the credentials configured for subsequent releases.
3. Confirm the bridge updates in place to the first Developer ID release. The first use of the existing `NexusCode Safe Storage` keychain item may prompt again. After choosing **Always Allow**, later releases with the same bundle ID and Apple team are expected to use it without another prompt. Users who miss the bridge and jump directly from an older install can install the notarized DMG manually.

Electron 45.1.0 pins Squirrel.Mac at `fffea30e`. `SQRLUpdater` obtains the current application's signature from `SQRLCodeSignature`, which calls `SecCodeCopySelf` and `SecCodeCopyDesignatedRequirement`. It then passes that requirement to `SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors` for the staged bundle. The bridge's explicit designated requirement is therefore the policy used to accept the next release. [Electron DEPS](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v45.1.0/DEPS#L10-L11) · [SQRLUpdater.m](https://github.com/Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac/blob/fffea30e4a339a7f7d69a3391314b72548d209bd/Squirrel/SQRLUpdater.m#L265-L275) · [SQRLCodeSignature.m](https://github.com/Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac/blob/fffea30e4a339a7f7d69a3391314b72548d209bd/Squirrel/SQRLCodeSignature.m#L48-L88) · [Staged bundle verification](https://github.com/Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac/blob/fffea30e4a339a7f7d69a3391314b72548d209bd/Squirrel/SQRLCodeSignature.m#L103-L128)

The Developer ID package signs loose Mach-O files before signing the app. The packaging hook updates the packaged agent manifest with the signed Darwin binaries' sizes and SHA-256 digests. SSH bootstrap uses those digests to verify the upload locally and on the remote host. Electron-builder notarizes and staples the app before it creates the ZIP for auto-updates. The release workflow separately notarizes and staples the DMG for manual installation. The Developer ID update feed describes only the ZIP, so stapling the DMG cannot invalidate the feed's checksums.
